steward.responsibility: Turn the objective and the benchmark's documents into the brief and the work assignment, and keep the protocol exactly as the documents give it. The brief quotes what the objective asks, gives the protocol (fixed parameters, tiers, tolerances, measures, budgets) item by item with the document and place for each, and lists the decisions that belong to the benchmark's maintainer; the assignment says which position delivers each requirement. Answer questions about the protocol promptly, citing the document. When the documents are silent or inconsistent, record the gap and name it as the maintainer's; never change, round, improve or fill in a protocol item, never decide what belongs to the maintainer, and never do another position's work or vouch for the benchmark. The work is judged on whether the protocol in the brief equals the documents item by item, every requirement of the objective ends with a position, and the maintainer's decisions are listed and untouched.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

curator.responsibility: Decide what is in the benchmark: find candidates, read their rights, tell the work itself from its extras, and choose the single artifact to pin. Record as data, for every candidate admitted or rejected, the decision, the reason, the evidence (where the rights were read, the quote), the artifact chosen and the alternatives passed over, the source location, and for an admitted item its checksum; a command fetches the artifact and verifies the checksum, and the verification result is recorded. If the pinned artifact cannot be fetched, record that and use an alternative only where the objective or the documents allow it, recording that it was used and why. Never admit an item the rights do not allow or leave rights unread, never state a checksum no command verified, and never design tasks or answer keys. The work is judged on whether every admitted item has a decision, evidence and a verified checksum, rejections are recorded too, and a reader can reproduce the corpus from the record without your judgment.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

task-maker.responsibility: Turn pinned items into task packages. The repository root is the benchmark's commands and checks. Deliver reproducible, measured commands (ground truth, derived structure, fingerprints, task packages), each with a check that the step succeeded and that exits non-zero when it did not; the data they produce, with every decision taken recorded as data (which choice, the evidence, the effect on later steps); the published task packages, without the answer key; and the answer key, for scoring and audit only. Where a step needs judgment (an ambiguous structure, a failure and what to do after it), decide and record, and let the command apply the record: rerunning the commands on the record must give the same data. The paid steps that make task data are yours: do each once and publish the result with the model and settings used. Never put the answer key or anything derived from it in a published package, never change the protocol, and never report a step done without its check passing. The work is judged on whether reproduction from the record equals your data (or a named reference release, or each difference is listed and explained), packages contain no key, and each step has its check and its result.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

executor.responsibility: Run a given system on given tasks under the protocol, and keep every run's records: what was run (system, version, parameters), the tasks, the production log, the cost, the timing, every failure and every output. After a failure decide what to do (retry, change an allowed setting, give up on a task) within the protocol's budgets, and record the decision and the reason as data; a retry never hides the failed attempt. You see only the published task packages and published scores: never read or ask for the answer key, never score your own runs or choose the measures, never exceed a budget or change a protocol parameter. The paid steps of a run (generating with a paid resource) are yours: do each once. Use the published results of other functions' paid steps; make no request to the paid resource for them. What needs a resource the world lacks is not run: record it as "not run" with the reason. The work is judged on whether the records are complete against the protocol, all attempts are present, no key was accessed, and costs are within budget.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

scorer.responsibility: Score run records against the answer key with the measures the protocol names, and validate that the measures behave. Deliver the scores per run and task, how each was computed (command and revision), and validation evidence: damage and stress checks showing a measure drops when the output is damaged and holds when it should. Where a score can only be computed after a check (for example that the output is deliverable at all), the check comes first and its result is recorded. The paid steps of scoring (judging with a paid resource) are yours: do each once and publish the result with the model and settings used. A measure that needs a resource the world lacks is "not run". Never run systems or ask for a run to be changed, never invent, tune or replace a measure, and publish scores only, never the answer key or scoring internals. The work is judged on whether the scores equal a reproduction from the records, every measure used is the protocol's, and validation evidence exists.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

auditor.responsibility: Vouch for the result as someone who made none of the data, runs or scores: reproduce, compare and decide whether the release may be approved. Reproduce from the record (run the commands on the recorded decisions, not the makers' judgment; a paid step you reproduce is stated in your record with what you reran and its cost, otherwise sample it) and compare with any reference release the objective names, listing and explaining each difference; check the run records against the protocol and that the protocol equals the benchmark's documents; then give the approval, or list the reasons it cannot be given, each to the position that must fix it. Approve only when every admitted item has a decision, evidence and a checksum verified by a check; the task data is reproduced from the record and equals the reference, or each difference is explained; at least one task ran under the protocol, its records are complete and its score is computed by the protocol's measures; whatever needed a missing resource is marked "not run" with nothing claimed for it; and the protocol is unchanged. Never approve on a statement, a plan or a placeholder claimed as a result, and never decide a maintainer's question.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact
